_doc: Housing of every town (world/townHousing.js). A town's dwellings are counted by type (settlement.housing.d: { type: n }), derived the first time from its people, size and era (mix[type], slack over its people). Each dwelling houses `people` (a family and its kin; × eraMult[type][era] for buildings that rise a storey higher in stone) and lets `rooms` rooms to lodgers (lodgersPerRoom each) — the soft room a crowded town finds before it sleeps in the streets. foot: the building plot it takes (a row house half a plot, a tenement one plot for three or four families). Plots: the town's building ground, its dwellings' feet plus free plots (freePlots[type] × the feet at first, edgePlots a week added at the town's edge while free plots are scarce (a village or a town half as many as its shortfall of houses, at least that), or as the town-growth code lays streets: TownHousing.addPlots). Builders: each `build.every` days a town short of room (capacity under build.aim × its people) raises dwellings (build.perWeek[type] + perThousand a thousand people), each `days` to build, its materials taken from the market's stock (a house goes up slower without them: build.bareDays). What goes up is TownHousing.nextDwellingType: the town's mix for its size and era, denser (row houses, then tenements in town and city) as its free plots run under denseBelow of its ground or its people crowd past denseCrowd. Effects of crowding (crowd = people ÷ capacity): past 1, lodgers take the rooms let (lodgerWeight of the harm), past capacity + rooms the rest double up and sleep rough (full harm): rent × (1 + rentPer × over, ≤ rentMax; under capacity × down to rentMin), sickness × (1 + sickPer × over, ≤ sickMax), fire × (1 + firePer × over, ≤ fireMax), welfare − welfare × over (world/townLabour.js), growth ends at over growthStop (world/economy.js growthRoom), and the welfare pushes people to other towns.

land._doc: How much building ground a town has (world/townLand.js): hexPlots plots on a hex of open, dry, level ground, × terrain[its terrain] (hills and mountains less, marsh less), less water[river] for a river through it and water[side] for each side facing sea or lake, less neighbours[settlement] for each neighbouring hex with a town on it and neighbours[field] for each held by an estate's fields, a farm or works, a rural site or the player's property (all in all at most neighbours.max). Beyond the ground a town stands on today, wood[terrain] of what is left is under trees: cleared plot by plot (clear: days of a crew's work a plot at the town's builders' wage, out of its purse into the woodcutters' and labourers' purses; woodPerPlot wood to its market) before it is built on. A walled town has only its walls' circuit (wallSlack × its ground when they went up, never more than the hex) until it builds outside them. Edge plots are laid only while ground remains. Recounted every recountDays.

redev._doc: When a town's ground is gone (no edge plots left to lay, under build.denseBelow of its plots free) and its people crowd past minCrowd, its builders pull down old low-density dwellings (from, in order) and raise denser ones on the plot (to[era]: the first allowed for the town's size whose people a plot beat the old one's by gain; a village builds houses only: village[era]), perWeek[type] + perThousand a thousand people a week, at most maxBuilding at once. The old dwelling's people are put out for the build: they lodge or crowd with the rest until it stands. Materials from the market's stock like any build; the crew (crew hands, the town's builders' wage a day, data townGrowth hire) paid out of the town's purse into the purses of its carpenters, masons and labourers.

suburb._doc: A walled town whose ground inside its walls is gone and whose people crowd past minCrowd builds outside them: a faubourg on its own hex when the hex has minPlots of ground beyond the walls' circuit (its dwellings poorer: mix; unwalled — crime + crime × its share of the town's dwellings; raided first — a sack or a raid takes raidMult × as much of it), else a new quarter founded on a free neighbouring hex as a village of its own (names: {p} the parent town), settlers moved from the town (settlers share of its people, min..max). Its streets are laid on the town's map beyond the walls: one for every dwellingsPerStreet of its dwellings, at most maxStreets.

satellite._doc: A town with no ground left at all (no edge plots, no wood to clear, its walls' quarter outside full too) and its people crowded past minCrowd or sleeping rough sends its overflow to found a village on a free neighbouring hex of its realm (not water, not peaks, no town, no fields, no works; the realm's or no one's): the overflow over its houses and rooms (or share of its people, min..max), real households of its roster among them, their share of its purse, grain and timber. At most one every everyYears a town, maxPerTown in all.

player._doc: What the player may raise on a lot of their own to let by the room (systems/lots.js buildTenementOnLot): cost[type][town type] gold, standing after days; each room let to a lodger at the town's house rent × roomShare a day (× the crowding's rent), a room taken at tenantChance a day (× the crowding) and left at leaveChance.
